name: GLOW
used_for: Marketed by research-peptide sellers and clinics as a skin, collagen, hair and soft-tissue repair blend. These uses are promotional claims, not approved indications.
summary: GLOW is a nickname for a three-peptide blend of GHK-Cu, BPC-157 and TB-500. No approved product contains it, and no combination-specific human study was found in the sources reviewed. A Florida wellness clinic's guide describes such blends as not standardized products and says a blend does not automatically have clinical evidence because its ingredients were researched separately. The detailed information is on the pages for GHK-Cu, BPC-157 and TB-500; formulations vary by seller. The combination's side effects are not separately characterized.

administration_guidance.text: The Peptide Dosing Protocols site (which carries supplier affiliate links) warns against combining separate-vial peptides in one syringe because of differing stability and pH needs, and says reconstituted solutions are refrigerated at 2 to 8 degrees C, with TB-500 having the shortest stability window of 1 to 2 weeks and BPC-157 and GHK-Cu up to 30 days.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: The Peptide Dosing Protocols site (which carries supplier affiliate links) lists injection-site irritation, short-term fatigue and occasional headache, and states the blend is not FDA-approved.
side_effects.label: internet

internet_claims.claim: The Peptide Dosing Protocols site says the name GLOW comes from the GHK-Cu component and associates the blend with soft-tissue repair, skin and collagen remodeling, anti-inflammatory effects and hair density.
A Florida wellness clinic's guide describes GLOW as a peptide blend rather than a standardized product and notes that human research on BPC-157 remains extremely limited.
